name: Banh canh Trang Bang
summary: The other Trảng Bàng bowl. Strands are milled from non-glutinous rice, partly cooked, then pressed into boiling water, with no tapioca added. The broth is pork bone, with hock, lean pork, blood cake or fish cake, scallion, and pepper. A price is Check on arrival.
origin: Trảng Bàng. The provincial tourism center says the bowl goes back to the early twentieth century, sold from shoulder poles on the road between Sài Gòn and Tây Ninh, and that kitchens have kept it for more than a century.
texture: The strands are off-white, long, soft, and still firm after they sit in the hot broth. The center says the partial cook is what holds them together, so the dough does not need tapioca or another starch. The smell it names is the rice itself.
taste: The broth is pork bone, simmered for hours, sweet and deep. A bowl usually holds pork hock, lean pork, blood cake or fish cake, scallion, and ground pepper. Greens come on the side. Dip the meat in plain fish sauce pounded with fresh chili, or season the bowl to taste.
howToEat: Stop for a bowl in phường Trảng Bàng, including along Quốc lộ 22, on the way between Ho Chi Minh City and the Holy See or Ba Den.

The Trảng Bàng town page and the older tourism article named bánh canh beside the rice-paper roll and did not describe the broth. The later article does. Both the naming and the later description stay.
A price is Check on arrival. The hour is Check on arrival. The center says the rooms are busy on weekends, holidays, and in the high season, and does not print a clock.
where: Phường Trảng Bàng and along Quốc lộ 22. Khu phố Gia Huỳnh is where the older article says the rolls and this bowl are eaten.
seoTitle: Banh canh Trang Bang — the rice-flour bowl
seoDescription: Rice-flour bánh canh in a pork-bone broth, with hock, lean pork, and blood cake or fish cake, in Trảng Bàng. A price and an hour are Check on arrival.
